title: Sunrise Kitchen
subtitle: Ayurvedic apothecary for everyday wellness
intro: The Ayurvedic kitchen is a living apothecary. Spices are medicine. Roots are ritual. Each ingredient carries a quality — warming or cooling, heavy or light — and choosing them with intention is one of the oldest forms of self-care.

ingredients.name: Turmeric
ingredients.use: Golden milk, curries, morning tonics, face masks
ingredients.note: Best absorbed with black pepper and a fat — the traditional ghee pairing exists for good reason.

ingredients.name: Ashwagandha
ingredients.use: Warm milk tonic, smoothies, capsules, moon milk
ingredients.note: Take in the evening — it supports deep rest and helps regulate cortisol overnight.

ingredients.name: Shatavari
ingredients.use: Warm milk, ghee preparations, morning tonic
ingredients.note: A gentle, deeply nourishing ally — especially supportive during transitions in the lunar cycle.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.use: Teas, golden milk, cooking, fire cider
ingredients.note: Fresh ginger is milder; dried is hotter. Pitta types should use fresh and in small amounts.

ingredients.name: Cardamom
ingredients.use: Chai, golden milk, oatmeal, rice dishes, desserts
ingredients.note: One of the few spices that is tridoshic — calming to all three doshas. Use liberally.

ingredients.name: Cinnamon
ingredients.use: Morning porridge, chai, golden milk, baked goods
ingredients.note: Use Ceylon (true) cinnamon when possible — it is sweeter and gentler than cassia cinnamon.

ingredients.name: Triphala
ingredients.use: Taken as powder in warm water at night, or capsules
ingredients.note: The most famous Ayurvedic formula. Not a laxative — it tones and rejuvenates the digestive tract over time.

ingredients.name: Holy Basil (Tulsi)
ingredients.use: Tulsi tea, fresh in cooking, infusions, fire cider
ingredients.note: Sacred to the Vaishnava tradition. Sipped as tea in the morning, it clears the mind before practice.

ingredients.name: Ghee
ingredients.use: Cooking, morning tonic with turmeric, drizzled on rice, medicinal preparations
ingredients.note: Considered the most sattvic (pure) of all fats in Ayurveda. Clarifying removes the milk solids, leaving a stable, clean cooking fat.

ingredients.name: Rose
ingredients.use: Rose water, rose petal jam (Gulkand), teas, face mist
ingredients.note: Deeply cooling and opening to the heart. A classic ally for Pitta types or anyone carrying emotional heat.

ingredients.name: Brahmi
ingredients.note: Named for Brahma, the creator. Traditionally used to sharpen clarity and calm mental chatter before meditation.

ingredients.name: Saffron
ingredients.use: Warm milk, rice dishes, tonics, golden milk variation
ingredients.note: A few strands in warm milk at night is the classical Ayurvedic Saffron tonic for mood, sleep, and ojas.

recipes.name: Golden Milk
recipes.subtitle: The classic tridoshic tonic
ingredients: 2 cups whole milk or oat milk
4 cardamom pods, crushed (or ½ tsp ground)
method: Warm the milk over low heat — do not boil.
Add turmeric, ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, and black pepper.
Whisk gently and simmer for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in ghee until melted.
Remove from heat. Add honey only after the milk has cooled slightly — heating honey destroys its enzymes.
Strain into a mug and drink slowly, mindfully.
recipes.ritual_note: Best consumed sitting down, without screens. The warmth settles the nervous system. Let it be a small ceremony.

recipes.name: Tulsi & Ginger Morning Tea
recipes.subtitle: Clarifying, immune-supporting, warming
ingredients: ½ inch fresh ginger, sliced thin
Raw honey to taste (optional, added off heat)
method: Bring water to a gentle boil with ginger and cardamom.
Reduce heat and add tulsi leaves.
Steep for 5 minutes — longer draws more bitterness.
Strain into a cup.
Add honey only once the tea has cooled enough to touch the pot.
recipes.ritual_note: Drink this before any food. Hold the cup with both hands. Breathe the steam before each sip.

recipes.name: Ojas Moon Milk
recipes.subtitle: A nourishing sleep tonic for Vata and Pitta
ingredients: 1½ cups whole milk or almond milk
method: Warm milk gently over low heat with saffron and cardamom.
Whisk in ashwagandha and shatavari powders.
Simmer on low for 4–5 minutes, stirring steadily.
Add ghee and stir until incorporated.
Remove from heat and add honey when slightly cooled.
Strain if desired. Drink in the 30 minutes before sleep.
recipes.ritual_note: This is a rebuild recipe — meant for seasons of exhaustion, stress, or nervous depletion. It builds ojas, the subtle essence of vitality. Take it consistently for 30 days to feel the shift.

recipes.name: Kitchari
recipes.subtitle: The Ayurvedic cleanse meal
recipes.season: Year-round cleansing, especially during seasonal transitions
ingredients: ½ cup yellow split mung dal (moong dal)
Optional: seasonal vegetables (zucchini, leafy greens, sweet potato)
method: Rinse mung dal and rice together until the water runs clear.
Warm ghee in a pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and fennel seeds — let them pop (about 30 seconds).
Add turmeric, coriander, and ginger. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add rinsed dal and rice. Stir to coat with spices.
Add water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 25–30 minutes until soft and slightly soupy. Add vegetables in the last 10 minutes if using.
Season with salt. The texture should be soft and easy — like porridge.
recipes.ritual_note: Kitchari is the one-pot Ayurvedic reset. Eat it for three days during seasonal transitions or whenever digestion feels compromised. It asks almost nothing of the digestive fire while nourishing deeply.

recipes.name: Rose & Cardamom Lassi
recipes.subtitle: Cooling, probiotic, Pitta-soothing
ingredients: 1 tbsp rose water (or 2 tbsp fresh rose petal water)
1 tsp raw sugar or maple syrup (optional)
method: Blend all ingredients until smooth and frothy — about 30 seconds.
Taste and adjust sweetness.
Pour into a glass. Garnish with dried rose petals and a dusting of cardamom.
Drink immediately while frothy.
recipes.ritual_note: In Ayurveda, lassi is considered the most digestible dairy preparation. Serve it at lunch, never dinner. The probiotics and cooling rose open digestion and calm the heat of a Pitta-dominant midday.

recipes.name: Triphala Night Tonic
recipes.subtitle: Gentle nightly detox — the long game
method: Stir triphala powder into warm water.
Let it dissolve for 1 minute.
Stir again and drink slowly.
If the taste is too strong, start with ½ tsp and build up over two weeks.
recipes.ritual_note: This is not a dramatic cleanse. It is a slow, steady commitment to digestive health. Taken nightly for 90 days, it quietly shifts bowel regularity, clears accumulated waste, and supports the tissues. It works in the background while you sleep.

rituals.name: Sunrise Ritual
steps: Wake before or with sunrise if possible
Drink one cup warm water with a squeeze of lemon or a slice of ginger
Tongue scraping — removes Ama (accumulated waste) from overnight
Oil pulling with sesame (Vata/Kapha) or coconut (Pitta) for 5 minutes
Nasya — 2 drops warm sesame oil in each nostril to clear the head channel
10 minutes of seated stillness or meditation before the kitchen

rituals.name: Seasonal Transition Reset
steps: 3–7 days of kitchari mono-diet to clear the digestive slate
Increase warm, cooked, simply seasoned foods
Reduce raw, cold, and dry foods temporarily
Take triphala nightly through the transition
Favor earlier, lighter dinners — finish eating by 7pm
Add 10 minutes of gentle walking after the main meal
